score_rationale: The verified precision characterization is a substantial theoretical contribution, while incomplete attribution of the supplied-graph benchmark and extensive presentation redundancy require substantial revision.
summary: The paper establishes matching minimax squared-risk bounds for total treatment effects under bounded heterogeneous additive interference, half-Bernoulli assignment, and independent calibrated edge retention. Its observable attaining rule and converse over the complete observation record deliver the stated consistency characterization. The principal claims faithfully reflect the verification contract, but the paper needs clearer attribution of inherited results and a more economical explanation of its contribution.
strengths: The characterization covers all admissible degrees and retention probabilities, including both endpoints, with universal comparison constants.
The converse accommodates every measurable randomized estimator using graph labels, assignments, and realized outcomes, giving the precision claim substantial scope.
The attaining estimator is explicit, observable, and accompanied by a useful assignment–audit variance decomposition.
The dedicated early related-work section distinguishes response classes, assignment mechanisms, and observation channels across several close comparisons.
The application discussion accurately frames independent retention as a prospective calibrated collection design, and the limitations section identifies concrete extensions.

findings.section: Introduction; Related work; Edge collection and the supplied-graph benchmark
findings.issue: The supplied related-work brief identifies CausalSmithKnownGraph2026 as the credited source of the sharper supplied-graph degree benchmark, but the manuscript substitutes internal references for that attribution. For example, “The sharper supplied-graph degree benchmark used here is stated in \cref{obj:thm:supported-boundaries}.” The comparison with SNIPE's cubic published bound, alongside this missing credit, leaves the provenance of the quadratic endpoint unclear. The discussion of Jiang et al. also describes its matched variance order without displaying the quadratic rate, which is directly relevant to assessing the estimator contribution.
findings.fix: Establish and cite the precise provenance and publication status of the supplied-graph benchmark at its first substantive use. State Jiang et al.'s estimator-specific variance rate with its assignment and influence conditions. Clearly identify the sampled-network precision characterization, complete-record converse, and joint consistency conditions as the contribution extending these comparisons, while crediting the supplied-graph endpoint.

findings.section: Global; Minimax precision and attainable estimation; Appendices
findings.issue: The manuscript repeatedly defines the same scale and rule, restates essentially the same frontier, and reproduces substantial arguments for the general and explicit frontier statements. Repeated descriptions of the complete record and consistency conditions further obscure the progression. Meanwhile, the main-text explanation of the lower-bound contribution largely names technical ingredients rather than explaining their statistical roles.
findings.fix: Organize the main exposition around one model, one estimator, and one principal characterization. Consolidate repeated definitions and narrative summaries, and use short cross-referenced deductions for overlapping consolidated results. Present each substantive argument once. Add a compact main-text explanation of the block construction: shared recipient responses, partially revealed source allocations, fixed unknown baselines, and the role of the count-constrained likelihood in accommodating outcome-driven learning.

findings.section: Testing bounds and minimax proofs — Combining the comparisons across degrees and retention
findings.issue: The sentence describing the equivalent expression says that the degree and collection contributions have “their sum bounded above by the constant-risk scale.” The uncapped sum d²/n + d/(nq) can exceed one by an arbitrarily large factor. The verified statement caps that sum through a minimum.
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with: “The equivalent positive-retention expression separates the degree and collection contributions and caps their sum at one.” Preserve the distinction between the uncapped contributions and the capped risk scale throughout the interpretation.

findings.issue: “Uniformly over n≥4, 1≤d≤n−1, and q>0” omits the upper endpoint restriction on the retention probability from the explicit uniformity claim. The verified parameter domain is 0<q≤1.
findings.fix: State “uniformly over integers n≥4 and 1≤d≤n−1, and retention probabilities 0<q≤1.”

findings.section: Population, causal target, and observation design
findings.issue: The model section interleaves schedule restrictions, published-model correspondence, assignment assumptions, audit assumptions, and the eventual additive-outcome definition. This produces substantial forward navigation. Several transition sentences also point in the wrong direction: “Outcome magnitudes are controlled by the following coefficient restriction” appears after that restriction, and the relation between measurement and assignment is described as “specified next” after the independence assumption.
findings.fix: Order the section as additive outcomes and causal target, schedule restrictions and class, assignment–audit design, observed record, and risk. Place the detailed published-model correspondence after the core setup or retain it in the appendix. Update directional transition sentences to match the final order.

findings.issue: The consistency sentence introduces d_n and q_n before explaining that they are sequences of degree bounds and retention probabilities, contrary to the first-use gloss requirement.
findings.fix: Introduce them as “degree sequences d_n and retention sequences q_n” before displaying the two convergence conditions.

findings.section: Observable estimation and supplied-graph comparison — Published-model correspondence
findings.issue: The published-model correspondence is registered as a lemma in the verification contract but rendered through a proposition environment in the manuscript. This creates an inconsistent formal-object kind despite the otherwise faithful statement.
findings.fix: Render the correspondence with the lemma environment while preserving its exact identifier, statement, citation locators, and generated Formalization scope disclosure.

questions_for_authors: Which supplied-graph benchmark results are inherited from CausalSmithKnownGraph2026, and what bibliographic version and locators establish that provenance?
